chapter.title: The Event Thread
chapter.para: A window belongs to the thread that made it, which runs its events; other threads must not touch it directly. A Rexx program with a user interface often has work done on other threads (a computation, a download) whose results must show in a window. BSF4ooRexx's answer, for JavaFX and Swing, is its AbstractGUIThread classes; this chapter describes the same model for .NET, in net.cls: AbstractEventThread, its subclass NetEventThread, and GUIMessage. Their names and arguments are BSF4ooRexx's, so that code written for it reads the same.

section.title: The Model
section.para: Rexx code on any thread sends a message to the event thread with runLater: the message (a target object, a message name, and its arguments) is queued, and a GUIMessage is returned at once. Later, the event thread runs the queue, in order, each message as target~messageName(arguments), and keeps its result, or its error, in its GUIMessage: m~result waits until it has run. While a message runs, other threads go on queueing.

Which thread is the event thread. .NET has no single user interface thread: each window belongs to the thread that made it, which runs its events through a SynchronizationContext (Windows Forms installs one when the first control is made on a thread; WPF's dispatcher too). The bridge notes every thread whose Rexx code has run with such a context: each is a user interface ("ui") thread, with its own NetEventThread and queue, and "later on that thread" is its context's Post, as JavaFX's Platform.runLater. Without a user interface, the event thread is the Rexx thread that waits in .net~nextEvent or .net~eventLoop (the "loop"): the queue runs there as one more queued call, so the same code works in a program with no window.

The class methods are BSF4ooRexx's: .NetEventThread~runLater(target, ...) sends to the event thread of target: the thread of its window, for a Windows Forms control once its window exists or a WPF object; else the default, the first user interface thread, else the loop. The instance methods send to that one thread: .NetEventThread~current~runLater(...). Waiting for m~result on the event thread itself, for a message it has not run yet, blocks it, as in BSF4ooRexx.

example.title: The event thread, without a window
example.programlisting:
m = .NetEventThread~runLater(.Adder~new, "ADD", "I", 2, 3) say m~completed .NetEventThread~kind .net~nextEvent(5)~dispatch -- this thread is the event thread here say m~completed m~result .NetEventThread~current
::requires "net.cls" ::class Adder ::method add use arg a, b return a + b

section.para: The project's samples show the rest: samples/rexx/08-event-thread.rex (no windows: runLaterLatest from another Rexx thread), samples/windows/forms-progress.rex (a progress bar updated from another thread) and samples/windows/forms-two-threads.rex (two windows on two user interface threads).

section.title: AbstractEventThread Class
section.para: The model, made general from BSF4ooRexx's AbstractGUIThread (BSF.CLS): an instance is one event thread, with its queue of GUIMessages. Subclasses give eventThreadFor and isEventThread, and a private invokeOnEventThread that has the queue run later on their thread; BSF4ooRexx's are FxGUIThread and AwtGUIThread, this package's NetEventThread.

section.para: Queues the message message for target, to be sent on the event thread, and returns its at once. The arguments follow, as for BSF4ooRexx: "I" and the arguments one by one, or "A" and one Array of them.

section.title: NetEventThread Class
section.para: The event threads of .NET: one instance per user interface thread, and one for the loop (), each made once.

section.title: default (Class Method)
section.para: Returns the default event thread: the first user interface thread's, else the loop's.

section.title: current (Class Method)
section.para: Returns the event thread that the current thread is, or &nil; if it is none: the way an event thread asks which one it is.

section.title: threads (Class Method)
section.para: Returns an Array with the event threads of the user interface threads, in the order they were seen.

section.title: eventThreadFor (Class Method)
section.para: Returns the event thread of target: the thread of its window, for a Windows Forms control whose window exists or a WPF object; else default.

section.title: isEventThread (Class Method)
section.para: Returns whether the current thread is an event thread: a user interface thread, or, when there is none, the loop's.

section.title: kind (Class Method)
section.para: Returns ui if the program has a user interface thread, else loop.

section.title: id
section.para: Returns the .NET id of the thread (ManagedThreadId); 0 for the loop.

section.title: kind
section.para: Returns ui or loop.

section.title: isEventThread
section.para: Returns whether the current thread is this event thread.

section.title: GUIMessage Class
section.para: A message for an event thread, returned by the runLater methods (BSF4ooRexx's GUIMessage, modelled after ooRexx's Message).

row.entry: Methods inherited from the Object class

section.title: completed
section.para: Returns &true; once the message has run, with or without an error.

section.title: result
section.para: Waits until the message has run (or failed), and returns its result: &nil; if it returned none or failed.

section.title: hasResult
section.para: Returns &true; if the message returned a result.

section.title: hasError
section.para: Returns &true; if the message raised an error. The error is kept in the GUIMessage, not raised nor reported.

section.title: errorCondition
section.para: Returns the error's condition object (as condition("O") gives it), or &nil;.

section.title: target
section.para: Returns the object the message is for.

section.title: messageName
section.para: Returns the message's name.

section.title: arguments, hasArguments
section.para: The message's arguments, an Array, or &nil;; and whether it has any.
